title: Minimax Welfare Regret of Exactly Harm-Safe Treatment Rules under Holder Smoothness
banked_reason: DECISION PANEL: REVISE — kernel_substituted@oeq:exact-log-frontier: the promised exact logarithmic minimax frontier remains to-prove; the nonmatching bracket is a weaker contribution kernel.
gap_reasons: The proposed exact logarithmic minimax frontier is not delivered: this node remains to-prove and the current nonmatching upper/lower bracket is a weaker kernel than the promised rate theorem.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 established a finite-sample all-policy reduction, an exactly safe upper policy, and a full-experiment lower bound giving a nonmatching logarithmic bracket. A targeted re-solve and independent maximality audit found no supported construction that closes the remaining factor (log n)^(1/(2s+1)); the exact-rate theorem remains open. D0.5 judged the delivered kernel below the field floor.
tldr: Kallus's sharp binary-harm endpoint and Jin--Egami's cutoff characterization specialize in the fixed two-stratum model to the optimal margin fraction \(0.4+2F(h)\), where \(F(h)=\int_0^1|h(u)|\,du\). The novel finite-sample reduction sends every exactly safe randomized rule to a bounded statistic whose expectation is at most \(F(h)\), explicitly charging core under-treatment, and makes welfare regret equivalent to the one-sided risk \(F-\mathbb E Q+\mathbb E(Q-F)^2\). The proved Bernoulli polynomial policy gives the exactly safe upper bound \(R_n\le C(n\log n)^{-\beta}\), while the full-experiment compact moment prior gives the all-policy lower bound \(R_n\ge c n^{-\beta}(\log n)^{\beta-1}\), with \(\beta=s/(2s+1)\). Their ratio is \((\log n)^{1/(2s+1)}\); the exact logarithmic factor remains open and no empirical H\"older condition is asserted for the Jin--Egami application.
gap: Jin--Egami establish finite-sample marginal harm safety and qualitative oracle welfare but no fixed-Hölder minimax regret. Li--Zheng--Cao--Geng--Liu--Wu estimate a policy harm upper bound and prove asymptotic normality and plug-in learner consistency, while Wu--Jiang--Luo--Geng prove large-sample properties for a sharp-upper-harm plug-in rule; neither result is a finite-sample minimax equivalence or an all-observed-policy converse. The closest integrated-\(L_1\) theory gives a logarithmically improved Gaussian upper rate and explicitly leaves the Hölder lower bound open. For \(s>1/2\), existing experiment-equivalence results are only asymptotic and do not by themselves preserve exact safety or the target regret rate; for \(s\le1/2\), their smoothness hypotheses do not cover the class.
fill: After recording the cited sharp-harm and cutoff specialization, the project extracts a feasible scalar statistic from every exactly safe randomized policy, establishes finite-sample equivalence to one-sided functional risk, and develops a full-experiment Bernoulli Hölder converse. The estimator wrapper and histogram policy calibrate feasibility, while the polynomial construction and multiscale analysis target the exact logarithmic frontier.
